summary.headline: Rubicon Q4 FY26 revenue rose 44% YoY to INR 5,139 million and PAT rose 111% to INR 768 million, with EBITDA margin guided at 22-23%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was about INR 5,140 million (+44% YoY, +8% QoQ), with operating EBITDA of INR 1,190 million (+64% YoY) and PAT of INR 768 million (+112% YoY). Full-year revenue reached INR 17,540 million (+37%) and PAT INR 2,467 million (+84%). Gross margin dipped slightly as the company leaned more on outsourced manufacturing to meet demand ahead of the Pithampur facility ramp-up. Management also announced the Arinna Lifesciences acquisition (85% stake, enterprise value INR 200 crore) and an ESOP pool proposal, and a board-recommended dividend of INR 1.5 per share.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 361 million (10.1%) in Q4 FY25 and INR 523 million (11%) in Q3

segments.name: Specialty portfolio
segments.commentary: Contributed about 33% of gross profit in Q4 FY26. Management says the pipeline continues to grow and new specialty launches are ongoing.

segments.name: Product concentration
segments.commentary: Top 5 products were 39% of revenue in Q4 (prior quarters 34%, 30%, 35%) and top 10 were 57%. Management describes the range as stable at 30-40%.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin guidance of 22-23% maintained for coming quarters, including ESOP, Arinna and Pithampur costs and raw material and logistics inflation; Q4 EBITDA margin was 23.1%.
Pithampur ramp-up expected from Q1 CY27 subject to US FDA inspection; management expects 12-18 months post inspection to reach decent utilisation of the general block.
Greater reliance on outsourced manufacturing expected for at least a couple more quarters, which weighs on gross margin.
R&D spend target of INR 5 billion over nine quarters (FY26, FY27 and Q1 FY28), with about INR 3 billion+ remaining after FY26 spend of INR 1,935 million; described as high confidence.
Capex of close to INR 300 crore across sites over the next couple of years; capex to lag demand.
R&D productivity assumed at 5x or more for subsequent R&D spend (FY26 actual updated to 5.9x).
Arinna expected to beat IPM growth in FY28; next few quarters focused on laying foundations before profitability.
Working capital days guided to stay around current range (126 days in FY26 vs 137 in FY25).
capex_capacity: Pithampur facility acquired (INR 149 crore, not yet commercialised); site qualified and product filings done, awaiting US FDA inspection date.
Capex in FY26 of INR 800 million (corrected from crore on the call); fixed assets rose to INR 5,726 million, driven by Pithampur and capex.
Management philosophy: capex only after sustained demand; outsourcing used short term to avoid losing demand.
Pithampur general block has enough demand to fill it completely per management; other blocks under work.
demand_pricing: Demand described as broad-based across older and recently launched products, with no single therapy area driving growth.
Pricing broadly stable, supported by portfolio and specialty mix.
FDA: 12 product approvals in FY26; 24 products under US FDA review; commercialisation rate 92% of approved products.
Gross margin slightly lower due to internal manufacturing constraints and higher outsourced manufacturing.
Arinna brings over 4,000 prescribers and an existing distribution network in India; Arinna FY revenue about INR 72 crore and EBITDA about INR 10 crore per analyst calculation on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Is the demand driven by specific therapy areas, and how much of growth comes from the top five products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand is broad-based across the portfolio, not limited to therapy areas or recent launches; top 5 share was 39%, within the 30-40% range.

qa_highlights.question: How long will Pithampur take to ramp up and what is the gross margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramp-up expected from Q1 CY27; the general block should reach decent utilisation within 12-18 months post inspection. No specific gross margin number was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory high and how much relates to upcoming launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory is high due to growth and new launches, including finished goods, raw material and packing material given long lead times; 24 filed products expected to launch over the next 1-1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 22-23% EBITDA guidance safe given raw material cost inflation from the geopolitical situation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, cost inflation (crude-linked) is factored in and EBITDA guidance of 22-23% is maintained, excluding unpredictable black swan events.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex guidance and what is the R&D productivity assumption?
qa_highlights.answer: Close to INR 300 crore capex across sites over the next couple of years; R&D productivity of 5x or more assumed for future spend.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost rise sequentially and will it fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance cost includes receivable factoring (about one-third of receivables factored); Arinna acquisition partly debt-funded, so finance cost may not fall.

qa_highlights.question: Is Arinna's India CNS business a shift in M&A strategy and what are its returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the focus is therapeutic (CNS), with India as an added market; Arinna's current scale is not the basis of the investment, and returns are expected to build over time.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from heavier reliance on outsourced manufacturing for at least a couple of quarters.
Pithampur US FDA inspection timing; ramp-up depends on approval.
Raw material and logistics cost inflation linked to crude oil and geopolitical tensions.
Inventory build (working capital 126 days) ahead of 24 products under FDA review.
Finance cost rising sequentially; Arinna partly debt-funded and INR 100 crore of IPO proceeds still unutilised.
Arinna integration and India CNS execution; returns on the INR 176 crore deal value are unproven.
Management declined to disclose product-level market share or therapy-wise R&D breakdown.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and demand visibility, but cautious on gross margin and guarded on product-level and Arinna disclosure. Management repeatedly declined to give product, therapy or acquisition-pipeline specifics.
key_quotes: We do expect a greater reliance on outsourced manufacturing for at least a couple of more quarters.
We will maintain the EBITDA, let's keep it that way, you know.
So, we are saying that this 35% to 39% is a certain range, so this top five, ten product will be in that range only.

adds.what: Pithampur facility (acquired for INR 149 crore), general block ramp-up subject to US FDA inspection

growth.why: Management guided only to an EBITDA margin of 22-23%, not revenue growth; Q4 revenue rose 44% YoY and demand is running above plan, but near-term supply relies on outsourcing while Pithampur (acquired, INR 149 crore) awaits a US FDA inspection date and ramps from Q1 CY27.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin guided at 22-23% for coming quarters versus Q4 FY26 at 23.1%, with ESOP, Arinna and Pithampur costs plus raw material and logistics inflation weighing; gross margin slightly lower on outsourced manufacturing.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Pithampur facility (acquired for INR 149 crore) is guided to ramp from Q1 CY27 subject to US FDA inspection, with 12-18 months to reach decent utilisation of the general block; the inspection date is still pending.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 44% YoY to INR 5,140 million and FY26 revenue rose 37% to INR 17,540 million; 24 products are under US FDA review and 12 approvals came in FY26, though near-term supply leans on outsourcing.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management already projects close to INR 300 crore capex across sites over the next couple of years and says capex will lag demand; utilisation was not quantified, so a fresh announcement beyond this plan is conditional.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held EBITDA margin guidance at 22-23% and gave no revenue guidance to raise; the margin range was maintained despite inflation.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Raw material and crude-linked logistics inflation, heavier outsourced manufacturing for at least a couple of quarters, and Pithampur FDA inspection timing could pressure the 22-23% margin band, though management says inflation is factored in.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: 24 filed products are expected to launch over the next 1-1.5 years, and the specialty pipeline has new launches ongoing, with 92% commercialisation rate on 12 FY26 approvals.

rows.label: Finance cost pressure from Arinna debt funding
rows.why: Finance cost rose sequentially with about one-third of receivables factored, and Arinna's INR 176 crore deal value is partly debt-funded, so finance cost may not fall.

rows.label: Working capital days at 126 vs 137 in FY25
rows.why: Management guided working capital days to stay around the current 126-day range, though inventory is elevated for 24 filed products and new launches.

rows.label: Arinna India CNS expansion
rows.why: Arinna (about INR 72 crore revenue, INR 10 crore EBITDA) brings over 4,000 prescribers, and management expects it to beat IPM growth in FY28 after foundation work in the next few quarters.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand breadth, the 22-23% EBITDA band and the Pithampur ramp, but cautious on gross margin from outsourcing and guarded on product-level data and Arinna returns; analysts pressed on raw material inflation, inventory build and finance cost.
